entries.subject: DAMIT 5926: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-5926.txt. Model 5926, version 2021-11-12, pole (74°, 63°), period 6.041319 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 218 ±3 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: Registered surface imagery
entries.finding: Included 2026-09-18 as the SPHERE photograph lens: 30 camera-1 deconvolved frames, 3 nights from 2018-07-08 to 2018-07-14, cast onto the ADAM mesh with cameras computed from the release rotation record, JPL Horizons and each frame’s header. Its registration is the published comparison recorded in zimpol-published-comparison. Earlier finding, kept: Shape uses the shared missing-imagery grid. DAMIT's viewer illustrations are not source surface maps; no albedo, photographic color, regolith or composition is inferred.

entries.subject: Other DAMIT shape solutions
entries.finding: The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 149: pole (72°, 60°), 6.04131 h, version 2011-03-26, archive diameter 204 km; 1821: pole (81°, 67°), 6.041321 h, version 2017-06-13, archive diameter 220 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: Independent shape, spin or scale evidence distinguishes these alternatives, or a changed release offers a demonstrably better supported model.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a computed-camera photograph lens
entries.finding: Decided 2026-09-18 by the published comparison instead: the lens is prepared from 30 camera-1 frames on the ADAM mesh with the rotation record read latitude-first, and ships on zimpol-published-comparison; the registration stage’s numbers are in the README. Earlier result, kept: Measured with the cross-frame registration test on 30 deconvolved ZIMPOL frames (camera 1), each held against a reference built from the body's frames more than an hour away, cast through the ADAM reconstruction with the survey's rotation record read latitude-first. Disc interior 1817 pixels (median); peak correlation 0.14 (median) against a mirror margin of 0.75; 2 of 30 frames decisive by the stated rule (peak at least 0.15 and margin at least 1.5), of which 0 peak within 5 degrees of the model. The frames carry no markings the test can register, so nothing in them confirms or refutes the rotation record's phase, pole or handedness; the silhouette gate that qualified Kleopatra cannot judge a body this round either. A photograph lens for this body would rest on the survey's record read by the route proven on Vesta and on five elongated bodies, with no check on this body itself; it is not derived until one exists. Checked 2026-09-18 for the published-comparison route, which reads a release record against the survey’s own Table A.1 pole. The table prints Thisbe’s pole as (350°, 116°), past the pole: the direction (170°, 64°), which gives the 21° obliquity the table also prints. The release record reads (74.0°, 62.8°), as DAMIT model 5926 states, and its two column orders lie 34.1° and 38.9° from the table’s pole. The record and the table describe different solutions. The figure decides: read against the survey’s released model as DAMIT model 5926 states it, the record reproduces Figure B.30 at our phase, so the figure shows the released model, not the table’s pole.

entries.subject: Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.30 as the registration of the SPHERE photograph lens
entries.finding: Measured with tools/objects/sphere-survey/setup.mts against Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.30, the survey’s comparison of these frames with its models. Outline overlap with the paper’s ADAM panels 0.972 to 0.978 at our phase, against 0.976 to 0.979 for our own outline drawn at the paper’s pixel scale; over a full turn in 10° steps it peaks at our phase in 5 of 6 columns, one step from it in 1. With the paper’s photographs 0.967 to 0.973. Turned in the image, our outline best overlaps the paper’s photographs at -2.0 to 4.0° and its model panels at -2.0 to -1.0°. The spin axis we project lies at 97.9 to 98.0° on the sky against 95.9 to 96.0° for the figure’s arrows. Native outline residual 1.541 px mean over 30 frames at our phase, the lowest of a ±30° sweep. The figure’s column labels were read from its pixels, and each names a frame’s exposure start to the second. The release rotation record reads latitude-first, 0.16° from the published pole.
